ds: Laundering of funds misappropriated or extracted by senior officials and their networks, often through complex corporate structures, family members, luxury assets and international banking. Detection depends on PEP risk management, source-of-wealth understanding and scrutiny of unexplained wealth relative to official income.

src.t: FATF, Laundering the Proceeds of Corruption (2011)
FATF, Guidance on Politically Exposed Persons (Recommendations 12 and 22) (2013)
World Bank StAR and UNODC, Politically Exposed Persons: Preventive Measures for the Banking Sector (2010)
World Bank StAR, The Puppet Masters (2011)

cn.rt: PEP family and associates park proceeds in deposits and buy property with large unexplained deposits; handled mainly face to face or via online banking.

rat: PEP-network proceeds via offshore structures, private banking, cross-border wires and property purchases.

ind.cx: A PEP or close associate holds assets, accounts or lifestyle spending far exceeding legitimate known earnings.
ind.fp: Wealth can come from inheritance, prior private career or family business.
ind.ds: Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
ind.cn: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means

ind.n: Accounts held via family members or associates
ind.cx: Funds and assets move through spouses, children, in-laws or business partners who have no obvious independent source of wealth.
ind.fp: Families commonly share finances and businesses.
ind.ds: Funds and assets move through spouses, children, in-laws or business partners who have no obvious independent source of wealth.

ind.cx: PEP-linked funds sit in multi-jurisdiction companies, foundations or trusts with nominee directors and no clear business purpose.
ind.fp: Wealth planning and estate structures are often legitimately multi-layered.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.n: Large inflows from state-owned entities or ministries to private accounts
ind.cx: Funds from government bodies or state enterprises arrive at private or personal accounts with no apparent contractual basis.
ind.fp: State suppliers and contractors receive government funds legitimately.
ind.ds: Funds from government bodies or state enterprises arrive at private or personal accounts with no apparent contractual basis.

ind.n: Prime real estate purchases in foreign cities
ind.cx: Acquisition of high-value property abroad through companies or relatives, inconsistent with declared means.
ind.fp: Wealthy individuals legitimately invest in overseas property.
ind.ds: Acquisition of high-value property abroad through companies or relatives, inconsistent with declared means.

ind.n: Adverse media on embezzlement or procurement fraud
ind.cx: Credible reporting or enforcement action links the customer or associates to misappropriation of state funds.
ind.fp: Media can be politically motivated or inaccurate, especially in repressive jurisdictions.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
ind.cn: Adverse media on customer or associates

ind.n: Rapid movement through correspondent or private banking channels
ind.cx: Large sums move quickly through several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, with no hold period.
ind.fp: Treasury and liquidity management can cause fast movements.
ind.ds: Large sums move quickly through several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, with no hold period.

ind.n: Luxury asset spending inconsistent with profile
ind.cx: High-value purchases of yachts, jets, art, jewellery or education by a PEP-linked customer not explained by known income.
ind.fp: Some customers have undeclared legitimate wealth sources not yet documented.
ind.ds: High-value purchases of yachts, jets, art, jewellery or education by a PEP-linked customer not explained by known income.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.

Establishes how a customer accumulated their overall wealth and corroborates it with independent evidence rather than relying on self-declaration. It is central to managing high-net-worth, politically exposed and high-value-purchase relationships.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

Applies corroborated source-of-wealth checks, senior sign-off, enhanced monitoring and sceptical review of public-sector links for politically exposed persons and their networks. It targets the corruption and misappropriation risk specific to these customers.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

ctl.n: Public-funds payment monitoring and contract evidence
ctl.ds: Flags credits from public bodies to personal or new accounts, atypical state-to-private flows and onward movement, and requires contracts and tender evidence for payments from state entities. It targets diversion of public money.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.
Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.
